XRequestId.description: The ID of the request, also in the log lines it wrote. A well-formed one sent by a trusted proxy is kept, otherwise the server generates one. Every response carries it.

Limit.description: Page size; the response then carries meta with total, limit and offset.
Limit.name: limit

Sort.description: A column name, prefixed with - for descending order.
Sort.name: sort

ApprovalRequired.description: 202: with the two-person rule on, the action waits for a second administrator (code approval_required, data.approval).

BadRequest.description: 400: the request is malformed or a parameter is invalid (invalid_request).

Conflict.description: 409: the request conflicts with the current state (conflict, busy, job_changed, protected, preflight_failed, sharded_unsupported).

Error.description: An error: the envelope with success false, an error text and a code.

Forbidden.description: 403: scope, role, connection access or CSRF refused the request (forbidden, approval_refused).

uri.description: Write-only credential-bearing URI; responses mask the password.

data.description: The payload; its shape depends on the route.

error.description: Human-readable error text; may change between releases. Present on errors.

message.description: Human-readable note, e.g. on a 202 waiting for approval.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error code, the closed set of internal/apierr. Match it rather than the English error text. approval_required is the code of a 202 answer, not an error. GET /api/v1/ready answers 503 with its own ReadyCode instead.

data.description: Extra detail of some errors, e.g. the checks of a refused preflight.

role.description: HA role; active outside HA mode.

ReadyCode.description: Why GET /api/v1/ready answers 503, in the order the reasons are checked.

safe_clone.description: Restore into <db>_rescue_<timestamp>; the default of user-facing flows.

csrf_token.description: Send as X-CSRF-Token on unsafe requests of the session.

s3.description: Secret keys are write-only; responses mask them.

apiKeyHeader.description: API key in the X-API-Key header. Needs no CSRF token.
apiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key

bearerAuth.description: API key as Authorization: Bearer mr_<prefix>_<secret>. Needs no CSRF token.

csrfToken.description: The csrf_token of the session; required with sessionCookie on POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE.
csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token

sessionCookie.description: Dashboard session set by POST /api/v1/setup, POST /api/v1/auth/login or single sign-on. Unsafe methods also need csrfToken.
sessionCookie.name: mr_session

info.description: Hand-written description of /api/v1. Every response uses the Envelope. docs/api.md holds the prose reference (field semantics, examples, edge cases); this document is the machine-readable contract. Resource schemas list the stable core fields and allow additional properties, which clients must ignore. A test keeps the set of paths and methods equal to the server's route table and the error codes equal to internal/apierr.
